name: Sale, standard rate 15 %
description: The general rate on a taxable supply made in Ethiopia
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 8(2) — VAT is imposed at zero per cent on a zero-rated supply and at fifteen per cent in every other case; art. 8(1) — it applies to taxable supplies by a registered person. Registration is compulsory above an annual turnover of ETB 2,000,000 (art. 12(2), or the amount the Directive sets). Electricity and water above the monthly 200 kWh and 15 cubic metres thresholds are taxed at this rate (utilities directive of 5 September 2024).

name: Sale, zero-rated (export of goods)
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 9 — a supply specified in Schedule 1 is a zero-rated supply; Schedule 1 covers the export of goods. The seller keeps the documentary proof of export the tax authority accepts. A zero-rated supply remains taxable, so input tax stays deductible.

name: Sale, zero-rated (export of services)
description: A service supplied to a customer outside Ethiopia
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 9 and Schedule 1 — the export of services is zero-rated; the proof of the customer's foreign location is documentary and is kept by the seller.

name: Sale, zero-rated (international transport)
description: International air or sea transport of passengers or goods
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 9 and Schedule 1 — international transport services are zero-rated.

name: Sale, exempt (financial services)
description: Interest on loans, insurance and other financial services
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 10(1) — a supply specified in Schedule 2 is an exempt supply; Schedule 2 covers financial services (the Regulation excludes legal, accounting and debt-collection services from the exemption). An exempt supply carries no output VAT and no input VAT is deductible against it.

name: Sale, exempt (residential rent)
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 10(1) and Schedule 2 — the letting of residential premises (and parking attached to them, per the Regulation) is exempt.

name: Sale, exempt (first 200 kWh of electricity or 15 m³ of water)
description: The monthly household allowance of electricity or water supplied exempt from VAT
legal_reference: Directive of the Ministry of Finance of 5 September 2024 — electricity and water supplies are taxable under the Proclamation of 21 August 2024 except the first 200 kWh of electricity and the first 15 cubic metres of water consumed in a month (bottled water excluded). The supplier splits a bill into an exempt tier on this code and a taxable one on ET-S-15; the core cannot split a quantity automatically, which docs/international.md records.

name: Purchase, standard rate 15 %, deductible
description: A local purchase at the general rate, used to make taxable supplies
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 29(1) — a registered person may credit the input tax on acquisitions made for the purpose of taxable supplies, supported by a tax invoice; art. 8(2) — the rate. Zero-rated supplies are taxable, so their input tax is deductible.

name: Purchase, standard rate 15 %, input tax disallowed
description: A passenger vehicle and its repairs, entertainment, or club membership fees
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 30(1) — no credit for input tax on passenger vehicles and their repair, unless the person deals in them; on entertainment, except in the cases the article lists; or on club membership fees for sporting, social or recreational activities. The tax is a cost: it lands on the account of the line and reaches no box.

name: Purchase, exempt
description: An insurance premium, or another exempt supply bought for the business
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 10(1) and Schedule 2 — an exempt supply bears no VAT, so there is nothing to credit.

name: Import of goods, VAT paid at the border
description: VAT collected by the Customs Commission on importation and credited once paid
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 8(1) — VAT is charged on taxable imports; art. 27(1) — the taxable value of imports is the customs value plus duties and fiscal charges; art. 29(1) — the VAT paid on imports is creditable. The tax is owed to Customs, not to the supplier, so it waits on 2125 until the import declaration is settled.

name: Reverse charged supply of services from abroad, 15 %, creditable
description: VAT the registered recipient accounts for on services supplied by a person outside Ethiopia with no fixed place of business there, and credits as input tax in the same accounting period
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Proclamation No. 1341/2024, art. 6(1) — a reverse charged supply is a supply of services made by a person outside Ethiopia who does not carry on a taxable activity through a fixed place of business in Ethiopia, to a registered person, Government institution or large unregistered person, that would have been taxable if made from a place of business in Ethiopia; art. 8(1)(c) and (2) — VAT at 15 % on a reverse charged supply made to a registered person; art. 8(8) — the liability arises at the time of the supply and is accounted for by the registered person receiving it; art. 2 — the VAT payable on a reverse charged supply is output tax of the recipient, and a reverse charged supply is a creditable acquisition; art. 29(1) — input tax credit to the extent the acquisition is for making taxable supplies; art. 52(4) — the recipient prepares a recipient-created tax invoice at the time of the supply. Both halves are in the same return: the base in RC and 6, the output VAT in RC (added to box 5), the input VAT in box 6
